first.rationale: The presenting symptoms (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the top of the self-serve funnel, and two independent inherited records converge there: memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields produced a durable first-week activation lift in SMB). That convergence is stronger evidence than any single record. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 says it buys acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention, which is exactly the wrong trade against a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective — it would move the headline metric while destroying the underlying value. Referral incentive (memory_57) is sound but addresses established customers, not the funnel that is actually degrading; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment entirely and does not touch the observed decline. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is a live second choice, but its recorded outcome is engagement and 'first meaningful action' — proxy metrics that may not carry through to qualified revenue — whereas the onboarding evidence reaches time-to-value. I am spending both verification pulls on the two records I intend to actually rely on rather than on the ones I am rejecting: memory_86 because its own caveat (raised early churn in complex-workspace accounts) is the single largest risk in my plan and I need the original record to confirm how that segment was defined and whether the churn effect was clean; memory_31 because a day-12 result is the oldest in the set and I want to confirm the 'durable' lift was measured over a real horizon rather than a first-week artifact, and that signup-field reduction is genuinely the same lever as onboarding-flow shortening rather than two things my predecessors merged. Key uncertainties I am carrying forward, not resolving: these memories predate the competitor's price move, so the population entering the funnel today may be more price-sensitive and behave differently than the accounts these results were measured on; the activation decline may be caused by that mix shift rather than by onboarding friction, in which case this experiment will underperform its priors. Guardrails: hard-exclude complex-workspace accounts per memory_86, and instrument 30- and 60-day retention alongside completion so I do not repeat the memory_73 failure mode of booking a top-of-funnel win that leaks value downstream. If verification shows memory_86's churn effect was broader than the complex-workspace segment, or that memory_31's lift was not durable, I will fall back to activation_messaging. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the segment-level harm is real but identifiable and excludable, so a guarded full test is proportionate — a broad rollout would risk exactly the population the record warns about.

final.rationale: Both pulls confirmed the inherited summaries and sharpened them. exp_86: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, with 60-day churn +9% concentrated specifically in complex-workspace accounts because the shortened flow strips setup steps those accounts actually need. That is a mechanistic, segment-bound harm rather than a diffuse one, which means it is excludable rather than disqualifying. exp_31: signup +15%, activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, with 30-day retention only -1% — the lift reaches revenue, not just a proxy, and the retention cost is small enough not to be a memory_73-style value leak. Crucially it did NOT replicate outside SMB, so the result is narrower than the inherited one-line summary implied. Final decision: run the shortened onboarding / reduced-signup-field flow on SMB self-serve accounts only, with complex-workspace accounts hard-excluded and held on the full flow. This is the one direction where two independently-sourced records converge on the exact funnel stage that is currently degrading (completion -4%, activation -6%). I continue to reject promotional_pricing as the response to the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 shows it trades 30-day retention for acquisition, which inverts the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue — matching a price attack with a retention-destroying discount would buy a headline number and lose the value underneath. Referral (memory_57) targets established customers and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) targets a different segment; neither addresses the observed decline. Uncertainties I am carrying rather than resolving: (1) both source experiments predate the competitor's price move, so today's funnel intake may be more price-sensitive and less like the measured population — the +4% qualified revenue figure is a prior, not a forecast; (2) the activation drop may be driven by that mix shift rather than onboarding friction, in which case this experiment underperforms and the correct read is diagnostic, not failure; (3) exp_31's non-replication outside SMB means I must not let a win here be generalized by a future session into an all-segment rollout. Guardrails: complex-workspace exclusion enforced at assignment, not post-hoc; instrument 30- and 60-day retention and qualified revenue alongside completion and activation, since 60 days is the horizon at which exp_86's harm actually surfaced and a completion-only readout would miss it entirely; pre-commit to reverting if churn rises in any segment beyond the excluded one. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout — the harm is identified and fenced, so a guarded full test is proportionate, but the pre-competitor provenance of the evidence does not justify shipping wide.
